title: Colorado's 4th Congressional District election, 2026
description: The 2026 election for Colorado's 4th Congressional District pits incumbent Republican Rep. Lauren Boebert against Democratic retired Navy Rear Admiral Eileen Laubacher, along with Libertarian and independent candidates. Boebert, who switched from Colorado's 3rd District to the 4th in 2024, seeks her third full term in Congress in a district that covers the rural Eastern Plains and southern Denver exurbs including Castle Rock and Parker. The district has a strong Republican lean, rated 'Solid R' by the Cook Political Report, but Democrats hope Laubacher's national security background and fundraising advantage can make the race competitive. The June 30 primary will determine the Republican and Democratic nominees, with Boebert and Laubacher as the presumptive nominees.
polling_note: No recent public opinion polls were found for the Colorado 4th Congressional District race as of mid-June 2026. The Cook Political Report rates the district as 'Solid R,' indicating limited polling has been conducted.

candidates.name: Lauren Boebert
candidates.summary: Lauren Boebert is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Colorado's 4th Congressional District, first elected in 2020 from the 3rd District before switching districts in 2024. A conservative Republican and member of the House Freedom Caucus, Boebert is known for her strong support of gun rights, opposition to abortion, and advocacy for limited government. She previously owned Shooters Grill, a restaurant in Rifle, Colorado, where staff openly carried firearms.

candidates.name: Eileen Laubacher
candidates.summary: Eileen Laubacher is a retired United States Navy Rear Admiral and the presumptive Democratic nominee for Colorado's 4th Congressional District. She served 34 years in the Navy, including deployments to Afghanistan, a tour as Senior Defense Official and Defense Attache in New Delhi, India, and a role as Senior Director for South Asia on the National Security Council. Laubacher graduated from the U.S. Naval Academy in 1990 and is running on a platform of service, bipartisanship, and challenging what she describes as a lack of serious representation in the district.

candidates.name: Douglas Mangeris
candidates.summary: Douglas Mangeris is the Libertarian Party candidate running for U.S. House in Colorado's 4th Congressional District. He works as a construction superintendent and firearms dealer. Mangeris is running on the Libertarian Party line, advocating for limited government and individual liberties.

candidates.name: Tim Veldhuizen
candidates.summary: Tim Veldhuizen is an unaffiliated independent candidate running for U.S. House in Colorado's 4th Congressional District. A resident of Loveland, Colorado, and a businessman, Veldhuizen is collecting signatures to appear on the general election ballot as an independent. He positions himself as a practical, independent leader focused on opportunity, safety, and responsible governance.
